scene.packages.core.src.scene-intentions: Bring coal into the home, wishing the household warmth and well-being
As the first visitor after New Year’s midnight, pick up your gift of coal, carry it over the threshold, and place it in your host’s hearth.
Pray for well-being for yourself and your family
Gently stir the seven herbs, scoop up warm porridge, and serve it in the bowl.
Send a wish for safety to someone you care about
Lift the square cloth, move it outside the window, then gently lay it down.
Send a wish for safety to the home
Lift the wooden bird pole, straighten it, then set it securely in place.
Send a wish for safety for the new year
Lift the prepared kadomatsu, move it beside the door, and gently set it down.
Send a wish for safety to your family
Lift the pair of ceramic bulls, move them toward the roof ridge, and set them securely in place.
Send a wish for safety to a child
Lift the prepared silver lock, move it into the gift box, and gently set it down.
Send a blessing for a wish
Lift the little mallet, gently shake it with a wish, then return it to the wooden rest.
Send a wish for a settled home
Lift and turn the miniature house to look at it, then set this vision securely in place.
Toss together, wishing for a plentiful, smooth new year
Dip the chopstick tips into the yusheng, toss it with your table companions, and let it fall back onto the plate while exchanging New Year wishes.
Stroke the forehead with a wish for success in study
Bring your hand toward the reclining ox’s forehead, gently stroke it, then draw your palm back.
Tie a thread for returning loved ones, wishing them safety
Pick up the white cotton thread, wrap it around the wrist, and gently tie it with a wish for safety.
Wave a branch with wishes for health and well-being
Wave the willow branch with a blessing, offer it to your host, and receive a thank-you gift in the basket.
Place it by the door with a wish to protect the home
Pick up the hiiragi branch, fit it with the grilled fish head, then place it beside the door.
Offer a prayer to the deities
Turn the tamagushi in your hands, entrust a prayer for your family’s safety to its leaves, then place it forward as an offering.
Offer clear water, wishing all beings freedom from suffering
Lift the pitcher, add water to each bowl from left to right, then return it to the side of the offering table.
Wish a new beginning health and happiness
Pick up the wooden mallet, gently tap the pre-loosened lid seam, then return it beside the barrel.
Pray for the well-being of all beings
Hang the complete prayer flag high above the ground, holding a wish that all beings may benefit and be at peace.
Pray for a good, sweet new year
Pick up the apple slice, dip it in honey, then lift it back to the plate.
Ask an elder for a New Year blessing
Slowly pour water over the elder’s hands, showing respect and wishing them well-being.
Pray for misfortune to turn to good fortune in the new year
Return the old wooden bullfinch, receive a new one, and set it in place.
Let the seeds in the pan smoke, then wave the cloth to disperse the smoke with a wish for your family’s safety.
Pray for freedom from illness and calamity, and safe growth
Lift the round grass tray, move it toward the gentle current, and let the paper dolls float away.
Bring New Year wishes to your family
Serve the cut New Year rice cake onto your family’s plates, wishing them health and well-being in the new year.
Offer wishes of happiness to a visitor
Lift the white silk with both hands and offer it to your visitor with wishes of happiness.
Send a child wishes for healthy growth
Lift the chitose-ame candy bag and offer it to the child before you, wishing healthy growth, longevity, and well-being.
Ask the mountains and lakes for protection
Carry a stone around clockwise three times, then add it to the ovoo.
Bathe the Buddha with a vow for all beings to be free of suffering
Lift the water ladle and pour over the infant prince statue’s right shoulder, left shoulder, then right shoulder, vowing to cease wrongdoing, do good, and liberate sentient beings.
Offer thanks to the deities
Add the white flower, lift the leaf tray of prepared offerings, and gently place it on the offering stand beside the field.
Keep a New Year intention of making merit
Lift the long paper-and-bamboo banner, move it beside the prepared sand pagoda, and secure the bamboo pole with an intention of making merit for the Lanna New Year.
Keep a wish to welcome New Year blessings
Lift the prepared paper with the fu character, move it before the home’s door, and gently attach it with a wish to welcome spring and blessings.
Keep a wish for protection from harm
Lift the prepared eye bead, move it toward the wooden stand, and settle its hanging loop with a wish for protection from harm.
Keep a wish for peace within the home
Lift the prepared decorative arrow, move it toward the wooden rest behind it, and gently set it down with a wish for peace within the home.
Prepare a plate of safety and abundance for the new year
Place the orange, green apple, and pear in turn to prepare a fruit offering for Lunar New Year ancestor worship, holding a wish for safety in the coming year.
Place the ruyi with wishes for things to go well
Lift the ruyi, move it near the wooden base, and gently set it down, offering wishes for things to go smoothly and as hoped.
Decorate the kumade with a wish to welcome good fortune
Place the three gold-colored decorations in turn to adorn the kumade, holding wishes to welcome good fortune and success in work.
Prepare a red horn gift with wishes for safety
Place the horn-shaped amulet and wish card in the gift box, holding wishes for the recipient’s safety and well-being.
Prepare twelve grapes to welcome a New Year wish
Place the three plates of grapes on the dining table in turn, twelve grapes in total, holding a wish for the new year to go well.
Hang a wish to protect the home and keep its comings and goings safe
Hang the three horseshoes on the small door frame in turn, holding a wish for the home’s well-being.
Greet the new year with wishes of health for loved ones
Lift the decorated branch, move it behind your loved one, gently tap and draw it back, offering wishes of health.
Welcome blessings into the home, wishing your family well-being
Push open the wooden door panel, scatter the roasted beans from the wooden masu outside first, then gently inside.
May Christ bless this house
Pick up the chalk, write the year, star, and C+M+B on the lintel, then put the chalk away.
Hang a wish for safety on a branch
Write a wish for safety, tie the wish paper to the plastic orange, then toss it onto a branch of the artificial wishing tree.
Send a wish for prosperity across generations
Stack the two round rice cakes and place the orange on top, preparing an offering to welcome the New Year deity with wishes for the family to prosper across generations.
Keep a wish for health to welcome spring
Lift the red-and-white spring cord already taken off, slip its loop over the flowering branch, and gently lay the tassel with wishes for health in spring.
Entrust a wish to the three stones
Pick up the stones marked 五, 大, and 力 and place them one by one in the omamori pouch, keeping them with a prayer to the deities.
Offer wishes to your family
Share a piece of wafer on Christmas Eve, exchanging wishes of health and peace with your family.
Throw the clay ball with a wish
Pick up the clay ball, aim at the square hollow in Turtle Rock, hold your wish in mind, and gently throw.
Entrust a prayer for financial good fortune
Lift the ladle, pour water to wash the coins in the sieve, then wipe off the water with the cloth, holding a wish for financial good fortune.
Pray for safety and health
Pass through the grass ring, circle left, right, then left again, and return to the front with thoughts of safety and health.
Tie three wishes into the ribbon
Tighten the ribbon’s three knots one by one at the railing, keeping one wish in mind with each knot.
Entrust New Year wishes for your family
Pick up the pomegranate, move it above the threshold, and drop it. Let the split fruit and scattered red seeds carry wishes for New Year luck and abundance.
Wish a child healthy growth
Unfold the cloth carp and pull the rope to raise it, leaving wishes for a child’s growth beside the carp streamer in the wind.
Offer blessings to the gift recipient
Think of the person receiving the gift, gather the cloth corners, wrap the gift box, and tie your wishes for them into this gift.
Prepare a gift for someone you care about
Think of someone you care about, gently wipe the wooden spoon, and place it on the display rest, letting this gift carry love and good wishes.
Entrust a wish for good luck
Add a pattern to the ceramic rooster and place it on the stand. Draw on its symbolism of good luck to hold a good wish for this moment.
Send love and blessings to someone
Think of the person you want to give it to, add icing to the colorful heart, and hang its ribbon, preparing a gift of affection for them.
Bless the gift recipient
Add a pattern to the colored egg and place it in the ceramic cup. Think of its recipient and keep a good Easter wish for them.
Wish peace and safety for the home
Assemble the paper-and-wood sun flower and hang it on the door frame, holding a wish for safety for your family and those returning home.
Wish harmony for the family
Join the straw diamond and hang it on the wooden frame. While quietly admiring the hanging garden, think of the family members you wish to bless.
Give thanks for a safe return
Raise the mast and place the model ship on its cradle. Recall a journey that ended safely and someone you wish to thank.
Reflect on the wish for safety in offering incense
Move the incense burner’s lid aside and place the thin incense stick. Before the light smoke, keep a wish for safety for yourself and those you care about.
Keep a feeling of thanks
Draw a stretch of the way home and a line of window light. Let this little picture of thanks hold the people and things you are grateful for.
Give today a moment of reflection
Shake the container, unfold the paper, and read this original reminder. Think of one small thing you can care for today, then put the paper slip away.
Thank the food and those who prepare it
Place the bread and colored egg in the Easter food basket. As you prepare it, remember daily nourishment and those who cook for the family.
Share spring wishes with your neighbors
Slowly stir the sumalak and serve it in the ceramic bowl. Keep a spring sweet for your neighbors and welcome the new year with goodwill.
Send thanks and wishes onto the water
Arrange flowers, light the candle, and gently push the leaf boat. Beside this little Loy Krathong floating light, keep a thought of thanks or a wish.
Wish for safety on this journey
Attach the little pouch to the travel bag with a wish for the journey ahead. On a return visit to give it back, leave a thought of thanks.
Offer a respectful greeting
Gently pull the bell rope and draw its end back. As the lingering sound fades, collect your thoughts and offer a silent greeting.
Pray for blessings for your family
Weave the straw cross and hang it over the door. Think of those at home and hold a wish for their safety.
Welcome the new year and its blessings
After trying the bamboo sieve’s rice-scooping use, hang the bokjori on the wall with a wish to welcome New Year blessings.
Leave a wish on the wooden plaque
Turn the ema over and hang it beneath the beam. Leave a wish or thanks before the plaque; you can also choose to leave it unwritten.
Entrust a wish for recovery
Wet the cotton cloth and tie it to a low branch. Keep a wish for recovery for yourself or someone you care about, then gently release.
Reflect on the reverence of offering light
Light the clay lamp and gently turn it along the arc. Reflect on the reverence of the light offering, then return the little lamp to the plate.
Keep a light for someone you care about
Place the candle and light its wick. Hold a petition, intercessory prayer, or thanks for someone you care about, and quietly watch the candlelight remain.
Set a wish or a goal
Paint one eye of the Daruma and hold your wish in mind. Leave the other eye for giving thanks when the wish comes true or after a safe year.
Tie a wish for someone
Make a loop, pass through it, and tighten the knot around the gift envelope. Think of the recipient and tie your good wishes for them.
Keep a petition or a thanks for grace received
Choose a little charm and hang it on the wooden stand. Recall something for which you wish to ask a saint’s help or give thanks for grace received.
Thank someone you respect
String the jasmine, secure the knot, and offer the garland. Think of the person you wish to thank, letting the flowers carry respect and gratitude.
Listen, and keep a moment of wakefulness
Gently strike the wooden fish and hear the sounds join. Let this rhythm remind you to collect your thoughts and attend to the present.
Tie a wish to a bamboo branch
Pick up the tanzaku and tie it to the sasa bamboo. Think of something you wish to improve, leaving a Tanabata wish.
Entrust a blessing to the lotus lantern
Gently push the lotus lantern with a wish. Quietly watch its light move higher in the scene, brightening this moment.
Pray for a safe summer
Gently brush the paper strip and hear the wind chime. Keep a wish for a safe summer for yourself and those you care about.
Pray with respect
Approach the torii and gently bow. Leave a prayer beside the ema rack, or silently keep it in your heart.
Pray for everyone’s well-being
Gently turn the prayer wheel clockwise, letting a wish for everyone’s well-being accompany the turning. Then stand quietly for a moment.
Quietly watch the midsummer wreath
Weave the wreath and gently place it on the water. Learn about its roots in Kupala divination of love and marriage, and keep a personal reflection as you watch it go.
Pray for world peace
Fold the paper crane’s wings and lift it before you, holding wishes for peace and for children in this moment.
